messages.text: England's Smith starts well at Baycurrent Classic as Bridgeman leads

metadata.summary: England's Jordan Smith enjoyed a strong start to the Baycurrent Classic with a bogey-free, seven-under 64 leaving him one shot behind first-round leader Jacob Bridgeman in Japan.
metadata.content: PGA Tour: England's Jordan Smith starts well at Baycurrent Classic as Jacob Bridgeman leads in Japan | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content PGA Tour: England's Jordan Smith starts well at Baycurrent Classic as Jacob Bridgeman leads in Japan Jordan Smith one shot off lead at Yokohama Country Club after bogey-free 64; pacesetter Jacob Bridgeman looking for second win in as many starts; defending champion Xander Schauffele one under after up-and-down day, watch second round from 4am Friday on Sky Sports Golf Thursday 8 October 2026 08:02, UK Image: Jordan Smith is one shot off the lead after round one of the PGA Tour's Baycurrent Classic England's Jordan Smith enjoyed a strong start to the Baycurrent Classic with a bogey-free, seven-under 64 leaving him one shot behind first-round leader Jacob Bridgeman in Japan. Smith, who has made 17 of 23 cuts and recorded eight top-25 finishes with a best of third at the Valspar Championship since earning a PGA Tour card for 2026, registered four birdies on his front nine and three coming home at Yokohama Country Club. The 33-year-old said: "I'm very happy. I wouldn't say I had my best stuff out there today but there was a lot of good short game shots, a lot of good putting. It was just a nice day out there." His unprecedented 12-month clean sweep may be over following a crushing 10-4 defeat by Jonny Clayton in the quarter-finals of the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam and a shock first-round exit at the World Grand Prix , but he can still qualify for next month's Players Championship Finals. The world No 1 had won the first six premier events of the season following his World Championship triumph at Alexandra Palace in January with the World Masters, UK Open, Premier League, World Cup of Darts and World Matchplay.
